title: Compact-support reduction realization with normalized open tensor comparison
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$, $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For every scheme $W$ use a small skeleton of $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$, completed coefficient sheaf $R_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$, and ordinary unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. On the vertical sequence site write $\mathcal Q_W(n,U)=(A_n)_W(U)$, $R_W^{\mathrm{const}}$ for the constant sequence ring, $\mathscr P$ for the one-point sequence topos, and $\mathcal A=(A_n)_n$ for its quotient ring [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]. Let $\rho_W:(W^{\mathrm{Tow}},\mathcal Q_W)\to(W^{\mathrm{Tow}},R_W^{\mathrm{const}})$ and $\rho_0:(\mathscr P,\mathcal A)\to(\mathscr P,R)$ be scalar restriction morphisms. Write $g_W^{\mathcal Q}$ and $g_W^R$ for point-sections morphisms to these one-point sequence topoi, with $g_W^R\rho_W=\rho_0g_W^{\mathcal Q}$. The symbol $Rg_*$ means derived sections with values in towers, without inverse limit. Restriction $\rho_*$ is exact. Use the derived internal Hom and signed closed tensor-Hom structure [def-pur-derived-internal-hom, def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model].
Let $k$ be a field with $\ell$ invertible, and let $a:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism between finite-type $k$-schemes, with a fixed compactification $X\xrightarrow j Z\xrightarrow pY$, $pj=a$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. On the quotient sequence sites put $F^{\mathcal Q}=Rp_*^{\mathcal Q}j_!$, with proper image derived after exact open extension, and $F_n=Rp_{*,n}j_!$ at $A_n$ [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. For $K\in D(R_X)$ put $V=\operatorname{const}K$ and $M=L\rho_X^*V$, with $M_n=K_n=K\otimes^L_{R_X}(A_n)_X$ and actual quotient transitions [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction].
There is a natural identification of derived tower functors
$$\rho_{Y*}F^{\mathcal Q}M\cong\mathcal T_a^c(K),\qquad \rho_{0*}Rg_{Y*}^{\mathcal Q}F^{\mathcal Q}M\cong Rg_{Y*}^R\mathcal T_a^c(K),$$
where $\mathcal T_a^c$ is the strict compact-support reduction-tower functor of [lem-weil-compact-support-reduction-tower-functor]. It is the coefficient-restriction comparison for the separately derived direct images and the actual open extension. With a flat-term K-flat $P\to K$ it has input the strict quotient system $(P\otimes_{R_X}(A_n)_X)_n$. Its evaluations are $\operatorname{Res}_nF_nK_n$, and every transition $m\to n$ is compact support of $K_m\to\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}K_n$ followed by the specified coefficient-restriction comparison. After point sections the evaluations are $R\Gamma(Y,F_nK_n)$ with the same transitions.
For arbitrary $U\in D(\mathcal Q_X)$ and $L\in D(\mathcal Q_Z)$ the open comparison used with this realization is the canonical natural isomorphism of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] for the ringed diagram topoi of the vertical sequence sites, with $j^{-1}\mathcal Q_Z=\mathcal Q_X$ including all quotient restrictions,
$$\gamma_{U,L}:j_!U\otimes^L_{\mathcal Q_Z}L\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!(U\otimes^L_{\mathcal Q_X}Lj^*L).$$
On a flat-term K-flat representative of $L$ it is represented by the sheafified module tensor isomorphism on each total-complex summand, $u\otimes l\mapsto u\otimes l|_X$, whose chain-level components commute with every quotient-semilinear transition. Hence its exact finite evaluations are the canonical open tensor comparisons over the constant ring $A_n$ of the same node [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. All comparisons here are transformations on the whole derived sequence sites, independent of representatives; no isomorphism of a tensor over $\mathcal Q$ with a tensor over the completed ring is asserted.

proof.text: Apply coefficientDerivedSystemEvaluationCalculus at X and at the compactification middle scheme Z, retaining the supplied reduction functor and its evaluation comparisons. The strict tower and whole-system realization remain the named composites already defined in this module.

Apply the native point-sections existence lemma to Y, and the native normalized open-tensor models existence lemma to the open immersion and the two calculi. These produce SectionsModel, the system and finite OpenTensorModels, and GammaEvaluation without adding hypotheses on derived inputs.

For each K and all m>=n, the unit_projection field of SX and the compatibility of the total-limit projections give the reduction transition square. Use the proved private compactSupportReductionTransition from the reduction-tower module, which derives it by applying the finite adjunction Hom equivalence. Apply compactSupportNativeSystemTransition to SX.reduction.obj K. Pasting these two squares with naturality of sfCompactSupportRestriction gives compactSupportFiniteSquare. Then use compactSupportCoefficientTransition_restricted and naturality of completed restriction composition; compactSupportCompletedSquare is exactly the remaining pasting equation. This proves compatibility of the specified evaluation, not an unspecified existential evaluation comparison.

Expand pointEvaluation into evaluated pointComparison, sections.evaluation and sections of evaluation. Naturality of coefTraceTransition moves the evaluated pointComparison past the transition. SectionsModel.transitions gives the point-sections transition square. Functoriality combines the last two factors, the transition equality from the preceding step rewrites their composite, and functoriality expands it back. Associativity yields the required pointEvaluation equation. Package the five witnesses and three conclusions.

lean.note: The strict tower is bound to the native reduction/open/proper/restriction lifting composite. Canonical point-square and finite evaluations are normalized by derived units, and open tensor comparisons by pure tensors, the open adjunction unit and signed total summands. Helpers package precisely the representative and natural-comparison clauses of this node; arbitrary unbounded first factors are retained. H4 interface diagnosis: lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization's Mode.systems Assertion.gamma is relative to Operations.tensorX/tensorU of ProjectionRestriction.TensorModel. That type supplies a bifunctor and simultaneous resolving-pair representative/descent data only; it is not the CoefficientClosedStructure with the prescribed internal Hom and CoefficientTensorModels used by CoefficientDerivedSystemTensors, and provides no conversion to those fixed structures or one-K-flat comparison for an arbitrary first complex. Its restrictRing, open restriction and chosen extension also use the localized-site presentation rather than the native varying-ring pull/extension functors. Thus Assertion.gamma cannot directly be used at the required tensor and functor types. OpenTensorModel is the representative refinement at those recorded native interfaces, not a second definition of tensor: restrictionPure fixes the ordinary restriction comparison, ordinary_inverse and summand fix its signed total representative, and derived_model fixes its localization. gamma_inverse is exactly Assertion.gamma_inverse's open-unit adjoint transpose, using the same exactDerivedAdjunction. Under representative-preserving tensor and open-adjunction comparisons the inverse transposes agree, hence adjunction injectivity identifies the transported gamma with Assertion.gamma. The source normalization and all unbounded inputs are retained without assuming equality of independently presented tensor functors.
